definitions.explanation: A large mammal with a long trunk, large ears, and tusks, native to Africa and Asia.

examples.japanese: {動物園|どうぶつえん}で{象|ぞう}を{見|み}た。
examples.english: I saw an elephant at the zoo.

examples.japanese: {象|ぞう}は{記憶力|きおくりょく}がいいと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: Elephants are said to have good memory.

examples.japanese: {象|ぞう}の{鼻|はな}は{長|なが}い。

notes:
COUNTER:
{象|ぞう}は{頭|とう}で{数|かぞ}える。(Elephants are counted with {頭|とう}.)
- {一|いっ}{頭|とう} (one elephant)
- {二|に}{頭|とう} (two elephants)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {象|ぞう}の{鼻|はな} (elephant's trunk)
- {象|ぞう}の{牙|きば} (elephant's tusk)
- {象|ぞう}の{群|む}れ (herd of elephants)
- {象|ぞう}に{乗|の}る (to ride an elephant)
- {象|ぞう}{使|つか}い (elephant trainer)

IDIOM:
{象|ぞう}の{様|よう}な{記憶力|きおくりょく} - memory like an elephant (excellent memory)
